rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the “necklaces” as the bark itself: people wore bark from sanctuary trees for protection; Mujahid, Ata, and Mutarrif b. al-Shikhkhir held this view.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالقلائد نفس القلائد فهو نهي عن أخذ لحاء شجر الحرم حتى يتقلد به طلبا للأمن قاله مجاهد وعطاء ومطرف بن الشخير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hady is any gift given without a stated return.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الهدي كل معطى لم يذكر معه عوض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jurists agree that a person who vows a hady must send its price to Mecca.
rows.anchor: واتفق الفقهاء على أن من قال: لله علي هدى أنه يبعث بثمنه إلى مكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Garlands are objects attached to sacrificial animals’ humps or necks, such as sandals, marking them as dedicated to God.
rows.anchor: وأما القلائد فهي كل ما علق على أسنمة الهدايا وأعناقها علامة أنه لله سبحانه من نعل أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Garlanding is an Abrahamic practice that survived pre-Islamic Arabia and Islam, and applies to cattle and sheep.
rows.anchor: وهي سنة إبراهيمية بقيت في الجاهلية وأقرها الإسلام، وهي سنة البقر والغنم.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet once sent sheep to the House and garlanded them; Bukhari and Muslim transmit the report.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: أهدى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مرة إلى البيت غنما فقلدها أخرجه البخاري ومسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shafii, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and Ibn Habib accept garlanding sheep, while Malik and the jurists of opinion reject it.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا صار جماعة من العلماء: الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور وابن حبيب وأنكره مالك وأصحاب الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers accepting the report that sheep may be garlanded, even if the opposing jurists had not received it or rejected its singular transmission.
rows.anchor: فالقول به أولى. والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar and Malik say cattle with humps are marked by incision like camels.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت لها أسنمة أشعرت كالبدن قاله ابن عمر وبه قال مالك.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii says cattle are both garlanded and marked, without distinction.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: تقلد وتشعر مطلقا ولم يفرقوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says cattle are garlanded but not incised; al-Qurtubi prefers this because cattle have no hump and resemble sheep more than camels.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: تقلد ولا تشعر وهذا القول أصح إذ ليس لها سنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists agree that one who garlands and drives a camel intending ihram becomes consecrated; mentioning garlanding in the verse makes it equivalent to ihram.
rows.anchor: واتفقوا فيمن قلد بدنة على نية الإحرام وساقها أنه يصير محرما

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet garlanded the hady and sent it with Abu, yet remained free of ihram restrictions until its slaughter; Bukhari transmits this.
rows.anchor: ثم بعث بها مع أبي فلم يحرم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيء أحله الله له حتى نحر الهدي أخرجه البخاري

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: Malik, al-Shafii, Ahmad, Ishaq, and most scholars hold that sending hady without personally driving it does not make its sender muhrim.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب مالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وجمهور العلماء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that anyone who offers hady becomes subject to the pilgrim’s restrictions until slaughter; Ibn Umar, Ata, Mujahid, and Saʿid b. Jubayr share this view, as do the jurists of opinion according to al-Khattabi.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: يصير محرما قال ابن عباس: من أهدى هديا حرم عليه ما يحرم على الحاج حتى ينحر الهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that sending hady itself consecrates a person also cites Jabir’s report of the Prophet taking off his shirt before mentioning the camels he had sent.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا بحديث جابر بن عبد الله قال: كنت عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا فقد قميصه من جيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report from Jabir continues that the Prophet had been ordered to garland and mark the sent camels, then realized he had put on his shirt and would not pull it over his head.
rows.anchor: إني أمرت ببدني التي بعثت بها أن تقلد وتشعر على مكان كذا وكذا فلبست قميصي ونسيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls the chain of the shirt report weak because it includes Abd al-Rahman b. Ata b. Abi Lubaba.
rows.anchor: في إسناده عبد الرحمن بن عطاء بن أبي لبيبة وهو ضعيف.

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans say garlanding a sheep does not make its companion muhrim because sheep garlanding is neither a Prophetic practice nor a rite, and a wolf may prevent it reaching the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فقال الكوفيون: لا يصير محرما لأن تقليد الشاة ليس بمسنون ولا من الشعائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha’s report says she made the garlands from ʿahn, meaning dyed wool; the phrase is linked to Qur’an 101:5, which compares mountains to fluffed wool.
rows.anchor: العهن الصوف المصبوغ ومنه قوله تعالى: وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش [القارعة: 5].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hady that has been garlanded or marked may not be sold or gifted because it has become obligatory; if its sponsor dies, it is not inherited and is carried out for its designated purpose.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز بيع الهدي ولا هبته إذا قلد أو أشعر لأنه قد وجب، وإن مات موجبه لم يورث عنه ونفذ لوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under Malik’s doctrine, an udhiyya is not obligatory until slaughter unless the owner verbally commits it; a verbally committed animal becomes designated and cannot be sold.
rows.anchor: فإن أوجبها بالقول قبل الذبح فقال: جعلت هذه الشاة أضحية تعينت

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: If a verbally committed udhiyya is lost but found during or after the sacrifice days, it must still be slaughtered; Ahmad and Ishaq say a replacement bought in the meantime is slaughtered too.
rows.anchor: ذبحها ولم يجز له بيعها فإن كان اشترى أضحية غيرها ذبحهما جميعا في قول أحمد وإسحاق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii says no replacement is due if an udhiyya is lost or stolen, because replacement applies only to an obligatory offering.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: لا بدل عليه إذا ضلت أو سرقت، إنما الإبدال في الواجب.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that a lost udhiyya has already fulfilled its purpose.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: إذا ضلت فقد أجزأت.

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: If someone dies on the day of sacrifice before slaughtering, the udhiyya is inherited like his other property, unlike hady; Ahmad and Abu Thawr require it to be slaughtered in any case.
rows.anchor: ومن مات يوم النحر قبل أن يضحي كانت ضحيته موروثة عنه كسائر ماله بخلاف الهدي. وقال أحمد وأبو ثور: تذبح بكل حال.

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awzai says the deceased’s udhiyya is slaughtered unless his unpaid debt can be covered only by selling it.
rows.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: تذبح إلا أن يكون عليه دين لا وفاء له إلا من تلك الأضحية فتباع في دينه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the owner dies after slaughter, heirs do not inherit the meat as property; they may eat or give it in charity as he could, but may not divide it as an inheritance.
rows.anchor: ولو مات بعد ذبحها لم يرثها عنه ورثته، وصنعوا بها من الأكل والصدقة ما كان له أن يصنع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before an udhiyya is slaughtered, its owner must replace it if it develops a defect; this differs from hady and is Malik’s doctrine.
rows.anchor: وما أصاب الأضحية قبل الذبح من العيوب كان على صاحبها بدلها بخلاف الهدى هذا تحصيل مذهب مالك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A contrary view requires the owner to replace defective hady, but al-Qurtubi judges the first view stronger.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في الهدي على صاحبه البدل والأول أصوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those heading to the Sacred House” means people intending it, from the verb ammama, “to intend.”
rows.anchor: يعني القاصدين له من قولهم أممت كذا أي قصدته.

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads “those heading to the Sacred House” in an annexed construction, comparable to “not making lawful the game.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: { ولا آمين البيت الحرام } بالإضافة كقوله: «غير محلي الصيد»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that believers must not prevent even non-Muslims who approach the House for worship and devotion.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: لا تمنعوا الكفار القاصدين البيت الحرام على جهة التعبد والقربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation holds that the prohibitions concerning polytheists, garlands, and those intending the House were all abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: ما في هذه الآيات من نهي عن مشرك، أو مراعاة حرمة له بقلادة، أو أم البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abrogation view cites the command that polytheists be killed wherever found and forbidden from approaching the Sacred Mosque after that year.
rows.anchor: فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم [التوبة: 5].

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd say polytheists may no longer make pilgrimage or receive sanctuary in sacred months, even if they offer and garland hady.
rows.anchor: ولا يؤمن في الأشهر الحرم وإن أهدى وقلد وحج روي عن ابن عباس وقاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Other scholars say the verse remains in force for Muslims, whom God forbids frightening when they approach His House.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الآية محكمة لم تنسخ وهي في المسلمين، وقد نهى الله عن إخافة من يقصد بيته من المسلمين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition applies in sacred months and other times, but the sacred month is singled out to honor it.
rows.anchor: والنهي عام في الشهر الحرام وغيره ولكنه خص الشهر الحرام بالذكر تعظيما وتفضيلا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets God symbols as His commands and prohibitions made known to people; Abu Maysara likewise says the verse is un-abrogated.
rows.anchor: وهذا يتمشى على قول عطاء فإن المعنى لا تحلوا معالم الله، وهي أمره ونهيه وما أعلمه الناس فلا تحلوه ولذلك قال أبو ميسرة: هي محكمة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says only the garlands clause was abrogated: people wore sanctuary bark and were thereby left alone, but that protection was revoked.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لم ينسخ منها إلا «القلائد» وكان الرجل يتقلد بشيء من لحاء الحرم فلا يقرب فنسخ ذلك.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets the verse as forbidding the blocking of pilgrims routes.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هذه الآية نهي عن الحجاج أن تقطع سبلهم.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse came in the year of the conquest, when polytheists arrived in Mecca for pilgrimage and umra and Muslims wanted to attack them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نزلت الآية عام الفتح ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة جاء أناس من المشركين يحجون ويعتمرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion concerns Shurayh b. Dabi a al-Bakri, nicknamed al-Hutam: the Prophet troops captured him during umra, and the verse was revealed before that ruling was abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان هذا لأمر شريح بن ضبيعة البكري ويلقب بالحطم أخذته جند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في عمرته فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hutam came to Medina, asked what the Prophet called people to, and said he might accept Islam and bring his leaders.
rows.anchor: أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة، وخلف خيله خارج المدينة فقال: إلام تدعو الناس؟

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warned his companions that a man speaking with the tongue of a devil would enter; he later said the man came with a disbeliever face and left treacherously.
rows.anchor: وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه: «يدخل عليكم رجل يتكلم بلسان شيطان»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hutam stole Medina livestock, escaped his pursuers, and left reciting a poem; the narrative continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: فمر بسرح المدينة فاستاقه فطلبوه فعجزوا عنه، فانطلق وهو يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses quoted from al-Hutam describe his stolen herd being driven through the night and depict him staying awake while others slept.
rows.anchor: قد لفها الليل بسواق حطم ليس براعي إبل ولا غنم ولا بجزار على ظهر وضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet departed in the year of the treaty, he heard the Yamama pilgrims’ talbiya and identified al-Hutam and his companions.
rows.anchor: فلما خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عام القضية سمع تلبية حجاج اليمامة فقال: «هذا الحطم وأصحابه».

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that al-Hutam garlanded the animals stolen from Medina and offered them at Mecca, so the verse forbade violating what was marked for God even when the offerers were polytheists.
rows.anchor: أي لا تحلوا ما أشعر لله وإن كانوا مشركين ذكره ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s command not to violate God’s rites supports requiring completion of all hajj acts even after a pilgrim invalidates the rite, followed by make-up pilgrimage the next year.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يترك شيئا منها وإن فسد حجه ثم عليه القضاء في السنة الثانية.

rows.speaker: أبو الليث السمرقندي
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi distinguishes abrogated sacred-month rules from the still-binding prohibitions on hady and garlands, and treats garlanding with intent as ihram.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { ولا الهدي ولا القلائد } محكم لم ينسخ

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take “favor” as trade profit and “approval” as what the pilgrims believed or hoped to receive from God.
rows.anchor: يبتغون الفضل والأرباح في التجارة، ويبتغون مع ذلك رضوانه في ظنهم وطمعهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the verse gently drew Arabs to the pilgrimage season so they might hear the Qur’an and enter faith; God abrogated the arrangement after year nine.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية نزلت عام الفتح فنسخ الله ذلك كله بعد عام سنة تسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many scholars read the post-ihram command to hunt as permission, but al-Qurtubi disputes that reading of the command’s form.
rows.anchor: وليس بصحيح، بل صيغة «افعل» الواردة بعد الحظر على أصلها من الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi argues that an imperative after a ban remains obligatory unless context or consensus shows otherwise.
rows.anchor: لأن المقتضي للوجوب قائم وتقدم الحظر لا يصلح مانعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The clause about hatred not leading to transgression is glossed by Ibn Abbas and Qatada as “do not let it carry you,” a usage recognized by al-Kisaʾi and Abu al-Abbas.
rows.anchor: أي لا يحملنكم عن ابن عباس وقتادة، وهو قول الكسائي وأبي العباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this usage, jarama takes two objects; the cited line uses “jaramat” to mean that something caused Fazara to become angry.
rows.anchor: ولقد طعنت أبا عيينة طعنة جرمت فزارة بعدها أن يغضبوا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash gives an alternative gloss: “do not make you deserve it.”
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أي ولا يحقنكم.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Farraʾ gloss the phrase as hatred causing people to earn a shift from truth to falsehood and justice to oppression; a Prophetic report says to honor trust and not betray even a betrayer.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والفراء: معنى { ولا يجرمنكم } أي لا يكسبنكم بغض قوم أن تعتدوا الحق إلى الباطل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The cited Prophetic rule says to return a trust even to a betrayer and not answer betrayal with betrayal.
rows.anchor: أد الأمانة إلى من ائتمنك ولا تخن من خانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is compared with Qur’an 2:194, which permits only an equal response to aggression.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية فمن اعتدى عليكم فاعتدوا عليه بمثل ما اعتدى عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also means earning: a person may be called his family’s breadwinner, and “ajrama” means acquiring sin.
rows.anchor: ويقال: فلان جريمة أهله أي كاسبهم فالجريمة والجارم بمعنى الكاسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem “Jarimatu nahidin” illustrates the sense of acquiring one’s sustenance; ṣalib means fat.
rows.anchor: جريمة ناهض في رأس نيق ترى لعظام ما جمعت صليبا

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says jarama and ajrama both mean “acquired,” while “la jarama” means inevitably or necessarily; the cited verse also illustrates this usage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس: يقال جرم وأجرم، ولا جرم بمنزلة قولك: لا بد ولا محالة

rows.speaker: الرماني علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says the root’s original sense is cutting; carrying, earning, and deserving derive from cutting something off or severing it from something else.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني علي بن عيسى: وهو الأصل فجرم بمعنى حمل على الشيء لقطعه من غيره

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil glosses the Qur’anic phrase “la jarama anna lahum al-nar” as meaning that punishment is truly due to them.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل: لا جرم أن لهم النار

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says jarama and ajrama are two forms with the same meaning: to acquire.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: جرم وأجرم لغتان بمعنى واحد، أي اكتسب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads “yujrimannakum” with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, still meaning “let it not cause you to acquire”; Basran grammarians recognize only jarama.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «يجرمنكم» بضم الياء، والمعنى أيضا لا يكسبنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shanaʾān means hatred; the noun is read with either a fatḥa or a quiescent nūn, and the construct means your hatred of a people.
rows.anchor: والشنآن البغض. وقرىء بفتح النون وإسكانها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse came when Muslims at Hudaybiyya considered blocking polytheists who were coming for umra in retaliation for their own earlier exclusion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: لما صد المسلمون عن البيت عام الحديبية مر بهم ناس من المشركين يريدون العمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading “an ṣaddukum” with fatḥa makes the earlier blocking the cause for which Muslims must not transgress.
rows.anchor: بفتح الهمزة مفعول من أجله أي لأن صدوكم.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read “in ṣaddukum” with kasra, Abu Ubayd prefers it, and al-Aʿmash reports a conditional future form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير بكسر الهمزة «إن صدوكم» وهو اختيار أبي عبيد. وروي عن الأعمش «إن يصدوكم».

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats the kasra reading as a future conditional, but says the fatḥa reading better fits the meaning.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فإن للجزاء أي إن وقع مثل هذا الفعل في المستقبل. والقراءة الأولى أمكن في المعنى.

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas reports that leading scholars of grammar, hadith, and inquiry reject the kasra reading; al-Qurtubi argues for the past reading because the blocking occurred before the verse’s revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: وأما «إن صدوكم» بكسر «إن» فالعلماء الجلة بالنحو والحديث والنظر يمنعون القراءة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With “an taʿtadu,” the verb is in the accusative as the direct object: hatred must not cause transgression.
rows.anchor: { أن تعتدوا } في موضع نصب لأنه مفعول به، أي لا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم الاعتداء.

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim and Abu Ubayd reject the quiescent-nūn form of shanaʾān as an irregular verbal noun; other grammarians say it is an adjective on the pattern of kaslan and ghaḍban.
rows.anchor: وأنكر أبو حاتم وأبو عبيد «شنآن» بإسكان النون

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats “cooperate in righteousness and piety” as a fresh, general command for all people to help one another do what God commands and avoid what He forbids.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: هو مقطوع من أول الكلام، وهو أمر لجميع الخلق بالتعاون على البر والتقوى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that one who points to good is like the person who does it.
rows.anchor: الدال على الخير كفاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another maxim says that one who points to evil is like its perpetrator.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: الدال على الشر كصانعه.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take birr and taqwa as synonyms repeated for emphasis, since every birr is taqwa and every taqwa is birr.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل: البر والتقوى لفظان بمعنى واحد، وكرر باختلاف اللفظ تأكيدا ومبالغة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says equating the terms is somewhat loose: birr includes obligatory and recommended acts, whereas taqwa means observing obligations; treating them as equivalent is figurative.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وفي هذا تسامح ما، والعرف في دلالة هذين اللفظين أن البر يتناول الواجب والمندوب إليه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says taqwa seeks God’s approval and birr people’s approval; combining both yields complete happiness and abundant blessing.
rows.anchor: وقال الماوردي: ندب الله سبحانه إلى التعاون بالبر وقرنه بالتقوى له لأن في التقوى رضا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad lists forms of cooperation: scholars teach, the wealthy give money, the brave fight for God, and Muslims support one another as a single hand.
rows.anchor: والتعاون على البر والتقوى يكون بوجوه فواجب على العالم أن يعين الناس بعلمه فيعلمهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The quoted Prophetic rule says Muslims’ blood is equal, their protection is honored even when granted by the least among them, and they stand together against others.
rows.anchor: المؤمنون تتكافأ دماؤهم ويسعى بذمتهم أدناهم وهم يد على من سواهم

rows.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says Muslims must withhold support from a transgressor and restrain him from wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ويجب الإعراض عن المتعدي وترك النصر له ورده عما هو عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sin” here concerns the legal judgment following crimes, while aggression is injustice toward people; the passage ends by commanding God-consciousness and warning of severe punishment.
rows.anchor: وهو الحكم اللاحق عن الجرائم، وعن «العدوان» وهو ظلم الناس

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: The occasion of revelation is a question from ʿAdi b. Hatim and Zayd b. Muhalhil, whom the Prophet renamed Zayd al-Khayr, about hunting with dogs and falcons when some prey died before they could slaughter it.
rows.anchor: نزلت بسبب عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن مهلهل وهو زيد الخيل الذي سماه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زيد الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “what has been made lawful to them,” “ma” may be the subject with “has been made lawful to them” as predicate, and “dha” is extra; alternatively “ma-dha” is a relative pronoun with the answer as predicate.
rows.anchor: «ما» في موضع رفع بالابتداء، والخبر أحل لهم وذا زائدة وإن شئت كانت بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyibat means lawful things, since anything forbidden is not wholesome; other glosses define them as harmless pleasant food and drink or properly slaughtered animals.
rows.anchor: وهو الحلال، وكل حرام فليس بطيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What you have trained” ellipses “the game of”: otherwise the wording would seem to permit eating the trained predators themselves, a view no one holds.
rows.anchor: أي وصيد ما علمتم ففي الكلام إضمار لا بد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some legal writers infer that the verse permits benefits from trained dogs and birds of prey, including selling them and using them in other ways, while excluding eating the predators themselves.
rows.anchor: وذلك يوجب إباحة سائر وجوه الانتفاع فدل على جواز بيع الكلب والجوارح

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: ʿAdi reportedly had five named hunting dogs: Salhab, Ghallab, al-Mukhtalis, and al-Mutanaʿis; al-Suhayli is unsure whether the fifth was Akhtab or Waththab.
rows.anchor: وكان أسماء أكلبه سلهب وغلاب والمختلس والمتناعس قال السهيلي وخامس أشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees on the conditions for a trained nonblack dog: it responds to release and call, stops when rebuked after catching prey, does not eat the prey, wounds it, and is released by a Muslim invoking God’s name.
rows.anchor: أجمعت الأمة على أن الكلب إذا لم يكن أسود وعلمه مسلم فينشلي إذا أشلي ويجيب إذا دعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a required hunting condition is missing, the ruling becomes disputed.
rows.anchor: فإن انخرم شرط من هذه الشروط دخل الخلاف.

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: Most scholars allow prey taken by any trained predator, such as a cheetah, falcon, or hawk; the word denotes an animal that earns or acquires.
rows.anchor: فجمهور الأمة على أن كل ما صاد بعد التعليم فهو جارح كاسب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root “jaraḥa” means to acquire, as in the verse about what people earn by day and the verse about those who have earned sins.
rows.anchor: ومنه الجارحة لأنها يكتسب بها ومنه اجتراح السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse uses “jaraha” to refer to what the hunter acquired, supporting the sense of jawāriḥ as earners.
rows.anchor: يذكر الجارح ما كان اجترح

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: “Mukallibin” can mean dog owners or trainers, as a teacher is the owner of training; it may also mean people who intensively train animals for hunting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه مضرين على الصيد كما تضرى الكلاب قال الرماني: وكلا القولين محتمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says “mukallibin” does not restrict the lawful predators to dogs; exclusivists’ argument from the word is not decisive.
rows.anchor: وليس في «مكلبين» دليل على أنه إنما أبيح صيد الكلاب خاصة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says prey caught by falcons or other birds must be properly slaughtered if reached alive; otherwise it is not eaten.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر فيما حكى ابن المنذر عنه قال: وأما ما يصاد به من البزاة وغيرها من الطير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar likewise says a falcon’s prey is not lawful unless the hunter can reach it alive for slaughter.
rows.anchor: وسأل أبو جعفر عن البازي يحل صيده قال: لا إلا أن تدرك ذكاته.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi take trained “jawāriḥ mukallibin” to mean dogs specifically.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: «وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين» هي الكلاب خاصة

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Nakhaʿi disliked prey from an entirely black dog; Ahmad knew of no one who permitted it, and Ishaq shared that view.
rows.anchor: فكره صيده الحسن وقتادة والنخعي. وقال أحمد: ما أعرف أحدا يرخص فيه إذا كان بهيما وبه قال إسحق بن راهويه

rows.speaker: عوام أهل العلم
rows.claim: Ordinary scholars of Medina and Kufa permit hunting with any trained dog.
rows.anchor: فأما عوام أهل العلم بالمدينة والكوفة فيرون جواز صيد كل كلب معلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Those who bar black dogs cite the Prophetic report “the black dog is a devil,” transmitted by Muslim.
rows.anchor: أما من منع صيد الكلب الأسود فلقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority answer that the verse is general and that the occasion of revelation and a report from ʿAdi support falcon hunting; al-Tirmidhi’s report says to eat what the falcon holds, but its sole transmitter Mujalid is weak.
rows.anchor: احتج الجمهور بعموم الآية، واحتجوا أيضا في جواز صيد البازي بما ذكر من سبب النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same ruling is supported by analogy: what a dog can do, a cheetah can do, with no relevant difference; the comparison is likened to sword and dagger.
rows.anchor: وبالمعنى وهو أن كل ما يتأتى من الكلب يتأتى من الفهد مثلا فلا فارق إلا فيما لا مدخل له في التأثير

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth criticizes hunting as something that can seem like falsehood despite being treated as legitimate.
rows.anchor: وهو ظاهر قول الليث: ما رأيت حقا أشبه بباطل منه، يعني الصيد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophetic instruction to release the dog and invoke God’s name entails intention and the basmala.
rows.anchor: إذا أرسلت كلبك وذكرت اسم الله عليه فكل

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik disliked hunting when done partly for sport, Ibn Abd al-Hakam allowed it, and al-Layth voiced a maxim criticizing how hunting resembles falsehood.
rows.anchor: فلو قصد مع ذلك اللهو فكرهه مالك وأجازه ابن عبد الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hunting without intending lawful slaughter is forbidden because it needlessly destroys an animal; the Prophet prohibited killing animals except for food.
rows.anchor: فأما لو فعله بغير نية التذكية فهو حرام لأنه من باب الفساد وإتلاف حيوان لغير منفعة

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars, the Zahiris, and some hadith scholars require verbal invocation of God at release; without it the prey is not eaten.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب الجمهور من العلماء إلى أن التسمية لا بد منها بالقول عند الإرسال

rows.speaker: جماعة من أصحابنا
rows.claim: Other scholars in the Maliki school and elsewhere allow eating the Muslim’s hunted or slaughtered animal even if the basmala was deliberately omitted, treating the command as recommendation.
rows.anchor: وذهبت جماعة من أصحابنا وغيرهم إلى أنه يجوز أكل ما صاده المسلم وذبحه وإن ترك التسمية عمدا

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik’s well-known view distinguishes deliberate omission, which bars eating, from forgetfulness, which does not; this is also the position of the regional jurists and one Shafii opinion.
rows.anchor: وذهب مالك في المشهور إلى الفرق بين ترك التسمية عمدا أو سهوا

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The hunter must release or urge the predator; an animal that starts hunting on its own without release or encouragement is not lawful to eat according to the majority and named schools.
rows.anchor: فأما لو انبعث الجارح من تلقاء نفسه من غير إرسال ولا إغراء فلا يجوز صيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason is that a self-starting predator hunts and holds the prey for itself, so the hunt cannot be attributed to the hunter’s release.
rows.anchor: لأنه إنما صاد لنفسه من غير إرسال وأمسك عليها، ولا صنع للصائد فيه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata and al-Awzai allow the prey if the hunter had taken the animal out for hunting.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح والأوزاعي: يؤكل صيده إذا كان أخرجه للصيد.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Most readers read “ʿallamtum” with fatḥa; Ibn Abbas and Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya read “ʿullimtum” with a ḍamma on ʿayn and kasra on lām, meaning instruction about predators and hunting.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس ومحمد بن الحنفية بضم العين وكسر اللام، أي من أمر الجوارح والصيد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawāriḥ means earners; the view that it means animals that wound and bleed is weak and contrary to the linguists, though Ibn al-Mundhir attributes it to some.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سميت جوارح لأنها تجرح وتسيل الدم، فهو مأخوذ من الجراح وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers say “mukallibin” with an open kāf and doubled lām, for dog trainers; the term can also describe trainers of other animals, hunters, or dog owners.
rows.anchor: و «مكلبين» قراءة الجمهور بفتح الكاف وشد اللام، والمكلب معلم الكلاب ومضريها.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads “muklibin” with a quiescent kāf and light lām, meaning owners of dogs; “aklaba” means that a person’s dogs increased.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «مكلبين» بسكون الكاف وتخفيف اللام، ومعناه أصحاب كلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb aklaba means a persons dogs multiplied, illustrating the reading as dog owners.
rows.anchor: وأكلب كثرت كلابه وأنشد الأصمعي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in “you teach them” agrees with jawāriḥ, a feminine plural noun.
rows.anchor: أنث الضمير مراعاة للفظ الجوارح إذ هو جمع جارحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that trained dogs and analogous land predators must obey when commanded and stop when rebuked.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف بين العلماء في شرطين في التعليم وهما: أن يأتمر إذا أمر وينزجر إذا زجر

rows.speaker: ابن حبيب
rows.claim: Most scholars require the same obedience from trained birds, but Ibn Habib says birds need only obey a command because they rarely stop when rebuked.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن حبيب أنه لا يشترط فيها أن تنزجر إذا زجرت فإنه لا يتأتى ذلك فيها غالبا

rows.speaker: ربيعة
rows.claim: Rabiʿa considers a bird trained if it answers when called, since most animals naturally respond to being released.
rows.anchor: وقال ربيعة: ما أجاب منها إذا دعي فهو المعلم الضاري

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii and most scholars require the animal to hold prey for its owner; Malik’s well-known view does not require this.
rows.anchor: وقد شرط الشافعي وجمهور من العلماء في التعليم أن يمسك على صاحبه، ولم يشترطه مالك في المشهور عنه.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii defines a trained animal as one that responds to release, returns when called, holds prey for its owner without eating it, and has done so repeatedly enough to be considered trained by custom.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: المعلم هو الذي إذا أشلاه صاحبه انشلى وإذا دعاه إلى الرجوع رجع إليه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii and the Kufans say an animal that repeatedly obeys and holds prey becomes trained on its third performance; others say after three performances it is trained and prey is lawful on the fourth, while another view counts one performance and permits the second catch.
rows.anchor: وعن الشافعي أيضا والكوفيين: إذا أشلي فانشلى وإذا أخذ حبس وفعل ذلك مرة بعد مرة أكل صيده في الثالثة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, Ibn Jubayr, Ata, Ikrima, al-Shafii, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, al-Nuʿman, and his companions say prey is lawful only if the predator did not eat any of it.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والنخعي وقتادة وابن جبير وعطاء بن أبي رباح وعكرمة والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور

rows.speaker: النعمان
rows.claim: This first view says an animal that eats has held the prey for itself rather than its owner; Abu Hanifa applies the no-eating condition to dogs and cheetahs, but not birds.
rows.anchor: لأنه أمسك على نفسه ولم يمسك على ربه. والفهد عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه كالكلب ولم يشترطوا ذلك في الطيور

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas, Ibn Umar, Salman, and Abu Hurayra also hold that prey remains lawful even if the predator ate some, including when only a piece remains.
rows.anchor: وقال سعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله بن عمر وسلمان الفارسي وأبو هريرة أيضا: المعنى وإن أكل

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik and his school, along with one Shafii opinion, accept the second view; al-Qurtubi calls it analogical.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مالك وجميع أصحابه، وهو القول الثاني للشافعي، وهو القياس.
